one_star_reviews.text:
I am fully aware that customer service can be different in Spain, but this restaurant — and especially the owner — was by far the rudest and most disrespectful experience I have ever had.

First, the waiter, who I later found out was actually the owner, took our order. My friend wasn’t eating and just wanted to have a drink, while I ordered a starter and a rice dish for two. He became visibly displeased that our order wasn’t big enough, quickly dismissed us, and walked away. This was on a Sunday, when the restaurant was half empty.

Then, after more than an hour had passed, another waiter came over to confirm my order. This is when we realized that the order had never even been put through. In total, I ended up waiting around two hours for my food.

At the end, I spoke to the owner because the food I was served was clearly rushed and the portion seemed noticeably smaller than usual. He was extremely dismissive and said something along the lines of, “This restaurant isn’t for people like you.”

Overall, the people working at this restaurant showed a huge lack of respect toward us. I would only recommend this place if you’re okay with waiting two hours for average-quality food and being treated poorly in the process.

one_star_reviews.text:
Antonio, the captain at Aventumar, was extremely rude and handled the situation in a completely unprofessional manner. We arrived on time and were already seated in the shade while the boat waited approximately 20 minutes for another group that arrived late.

The boat was also extremely overcrowded. There were initially 16 of us onboard, and by the time everyone was accommodated there were approximately 22 people on a boat that appeared to have seating for only about 10 to 12 people. There simply was not enough sitting room for everyone. They were so oversold that they actually had to request two additional SUP boards to be delivered to us by another boat, and we then had to go two people to a SUP.

When the late group finally arrived, the captain initially told one of the women to sit in the sun. She refused. He then asked us to shift in the opposite direction, which meant moving us out of the shade and into the sun so that she could be accommodated. I explained that this made no sense. We had arrived on time and were already seated in the shade. The exact same amount of space could have been created by asking the people on the other end to shift toward the shade instead of making us move into the sun.

Rather than listening or handling the situation diplomatically, Antonio told me that I could move or get off the boat. As I tried to explain why I felt his request was unreasonable, he actually told me to “shush.” At that point I stopped speaking because I felt extremely disrespected and genuinely could not believe the way I was being treated.

What made the situation even worse was that although I stopped talking, he did not. He continued the confrontation and then brought the issue to the front of the boat, announcing that he was the captain, that he had been doing this for 20 years, and making it clear that it was his way or no way. The situation became so unnecessary and uncomfortable that Clara, his helper, eventually had to step in and make an announcement to move things along.

The issue was never simply about shifting seats. It was the captain’s attitude and the way he chose to accommodate a group that arrived 20 minutes late at the expense of passengers who had arrived on time. We were being asked to give up the shaded seats we had already been occupying and move into the sun, even though there was another way to create exactly the same amount of space.

I also came away with the uncomfortable impression that there may have been preferential treatment toward this particular family based on their background. I cannot know what his motivation was, but the difference in the way we were treated was noticeable enough to leave that impression.

Between the severe overcrowding, not having enough seating room, needing additional SUP boards brought out by another boat, being told to move or get off, being told to “shush” when I tried to explain myself, and then having the captain continue the confrontation in front of the entire boat, this was an incredibly unpleasant experience. I have rarely felt so disrespected by someone providing a service.

Very bad experience

My experience with ALSA was terrible from beginning to end. The bus arrived late, and instead of receiving any explanation or apology, the driver's behavior left much to be desired. His attitude was completely unpleasant, unprofessional, and showed an absolute lack of empathy towards the passengers.

I understand that delays can occur due to circumstances beyond the company's control, but the least I expect is respect, courtesy, and proper treatment. In this case, that was not the case. It felt as if the passengers were a nuisance and that it didn't matter at all whether we were waiting or had other commitments.

After paying for a service, I find this kind of treatment unacceptable. A terrible and very disappointing experience. I would certainly think twice before traveling with ALSA again and would not recommend this service after what happened.

Poor experience with the vehicle collection process

I used Aena's VIP Parking service at Málaga Airport and unfortunately had a very disappointing experience with the arrival and vehicle handover process.

When I arrived at the airport, it was not clear where I was supposed to meet the person collecting my car. Despite having a confirmed booking, the information provided beforehand did not clearly explain the process.

I ended up waiting around 40 minutes while trying to contact Aena to find out what was happening.

My biggest concern was the actual handover. The person who eventually came to collect the vehicle had no visible identification confirming who they were or that they represented the parking service. They simply had our vehicle registration written on a piece of paper.

When you're handing over your car keys to somebody at an airport, I think it's reasonable to expect clear identification and a professional, organised handover process.

I subsequently contacted Aena about my experience. Although they acknowledged my complaint and said they were dealing with it, I have not received a satisfactory resolution.

The whole experience caused unnecessary stress at the beginning of our journey. I expected considerably better organisation and communication from an official airport parking service.

one_star_reviews.text:
A dreadful experience, complete lack of control, and a profound lack of humanity.

Our experience at this center has been a true nightmare from beginning to end. We pay a monthly fee of €3,000 expecting professional care for our uncle, but instead, we've encountered appalling management, chaos, and a serious lack of empathy. To summarize:

Lack of medical oversight and serious negligence:

Medication management: They don't maintain adequate records. When we transferred him to another residence, they gave us incomplete documentation, and vital medication was missing. We had to travel and insist repeatedly to get a critical medication that we couldn't obtain at the pharmacy, even if we paid for it, because it was listed as discontinued.

Medical appointments and transfers: Medical appointments were missed due to disastrous management of coverage and ambulance requests. They also failed to pick up the necessary pre-test medication required for blood tests.

Documentation and reports: A complete lack of transparency. They gave us incomplete medical reports and don't inform family members about anything. No communication whatsoever from the moment he was admitted.

Degrading treatment and poor care: The care you receive as a family member is a lottery, depending on who attends to you, or how they like you. They lie when you ask for explanations and blame the resident to wash their hands of the matter.
We verified that our uncle was telling the truth.
The most shocking thing was witnessing Soraya (we believe she's part of the management) publicly reprimand him in front of the other residents, subjecting him to unacceptable humiliation, as if he were in a school.

We had seen negative reviews, but we didn't think the reality was so bad.
We were forced to move him to another residence urgently. Given this lack of professionalism and humanity, we are already taking the corresponding administrative measures by filing a complaint with the Ministry of Health and the Social Services Inspectorate. We recommend that other users who have experienced this take the same steps to prevent these situations from happening to our relatives in the future.

We do not recommend this center under any circumstances.

⭐ 1/5 — Very poor management and lack of professionalism in the cleaning service

My experience with this cleaning service has been very negative, and it's not the first time something like this has happened to me.

I contacted the company because I'm in the middle of moving and needed to arrange for my apartment to be cleaned. On Tuesday, I spoke with the person who apparently manages the service, and we agreed that a worker, who had been specifically recommended to me, would come on Monday.

My surprise came on Friday afternoon when it wasn't the company manager who contacted me to inform me of any changes, but rather the worker herself, Ángela, via WhatsApp. She explained that she couldn't come on Monday because, according to her schedule, she was free that day, and that she couldn't come the following day either because she already had another job assigned the previous week.

In other words, the company had confirmed a service with me for a day on which the worker apparently wasn't even available. And yet, the company didn't contact me to explain, apologize, or offer an alternative.

Furthermore, I'm concerned that my phone number, which I provided to the company to arrange the service, was given directly to an employee without my prior knowledge, especially since that person wasn't even going to perform the service. I believe they should also review how they manage and communicate their customers' contact information.

What's most worrying is that this isn't an isolated incident. About seven months ago, I hired another window cleaning service. Initially, they told me two workers would come, and then, on the same day, they informed me that one of them couldn't come because his father was supposedly ill. When I was later able to discuss this with the worker himself, he was completely unaware of the situation and told me he had been working elsewhere.

Therefore, after two similar experiences, my impression as a customer is one of a tremendous lack of organization, transparency, and professionalism on the part of those managing the service.

What's most concerning is that this isn't an isolated incident. I want to make it clear that my criticism is NOT directed at the employees. In fact, I believe they can be excellent professionals, and I find it unfair that they end up having to explain to the client organizational problems that are the company's responsibility.

An organization with such an important social purpose should pay special attention to its professionalism, transparency, and the way it treats both its clients and its employees.

In my case, after what happened on two separate occasions, I would not use their cleaning service again.

Terrible experience and total incompetence. I took my car in for an emergency repair because the gear shift rod broke. They charged me €15 to literally put on two cable ties, which broke two hours after I left the shop. Then I took it back for an engine problem. They charged me €35 for the diagnostic and told me the lambda sensor was faulty. I paid €220 to have it replaced, but after 9 hours the light came back on. I took it back and they told me it was the temperature sensor; I paid another €66 to replace it and the light stayed on. Now they're telling me it's the lambda sensor again and making me wait 7 days to look at it again. A real money-grab that blindly replaces parts at the customer's expense without solving the problem.

And on top of that, they're unpleasant and rude. Not recommended at all.

one_star_reviews.text:
We went to the cemetery with the children and arrived 10 minutes late. We entered without permission, and the man in charge of the grounds, very agitated, kicked us out.
There are many ways to say things, always with respect and courtesy.

The staff working in a place like this should be much better at treating families who come to remember their loved ones. It's not the first time this has happened to me, but today I found it utterly shameful, and I'm not going to let the poor manners of the woman working there go unmentioned. Without even a greeting, she told me from a distance, raising her voice in a rather unpleasant tone, right at the entrance, that it closed at 2:00 PM, which shocked me because we had only just arrived at the cemetery at 12:50 PM. It seemed she was in a hurry to leave or didn't want more people coming in. She didn't even greet us; she practically spat the closing time at us, as if to tell us to leave. This is a place of respect, where families go to pay their respects, to meet with a relative, to have a moment of peace remembering, and I think the staff should have empathy for the visitors. If they lack that capacity, they should go mushroom hunting. And I hope this review doesn't just go unanswered and that action is taken, at the very least, that they have a conversation with that woman.

The apartment was described on Booking.com as offering ‘stunning sea views’ - it does not offer any sea views, just a view north into the buildings of Calle Real.
The sun doesn’t shine into the apartment.

Their products are more expensive than even better products in Jaen. The "fresh pressed this week" we bought from them recently turned out to be old and certainly starting to reveal signs of rancidness after only six months even though we store it in a cool (<16C) dark place with no light. Clearly sold us old oil for the price of " fresh just pressed"! Very disappointing since we bought a large quantity at a steep price. Stay clear of this establishment that seems to not worry about honesty nor quality of what they sell.

I cant tell you how bad almost every bit of the experience was. I initially booked through ‘do you Spain’

I’ll number all the bad points as they occurred

1) rented a car seat and a booster seat. It Wasn’t until very late in the process that we realised costs  quoted are per day and not per hire.

2)landed at the collection point. Rep behind the counter produced a small bit of paper saying we weren’t insured through the agency - or rather we were only insured for personal injury. Not the car. Just as we were about to pay the unexpected extra fee for insurance , we saw emails from our booking warning us they would attempt this. We were insured and we would have paid for insurance twice.

3) after completing the collection we were pointed in the direction of the car. It wasn’t what we selected when we did the booking and struggled to for our luggage in the car. It was also a cheaper make and model.

4) the car was covered in scratches and dinks. Frustrating as they would no doubt have charged previous rentals for these repairs which weren’t  carried out.

5) we then picked up the car seats for our 4 and 7 year old. Both seats offered were too big for our children. We paid for a child seat and a booster seat. Received 2 boosters but with one being for larger kids. It didn’t feel safe but were told this is what they had.

6) as we set off we hoped to use our iPhone as a sat nav. The car had car play but only when wired in. Luckily we had the cable required with us. However when we used it the usb port wasn’t working meaning we had no satnav. After travelling for close to 12 hours and with an hour plus journey ahead of us, this also prevented us from charging the phone.

7) as you’d expect cars and notably windshields can get very dusty. Shortly into the journey we tried to use the screen wash to discover it was empty.

I struggle to see one bit of the whole process which was t tainted in some way

one_star_reviews.text: The dirtiest and most neglected house I've ever rented. When you arrive to give the rent money to the owner, everything seems acceptable at first glance, but after a while, you start to uncover the truth. Walking barefoot for the first two minutes, I noticed the floor was dirty, so we started mopping. When we got the cleaning supplies from a cupboard where they were stored, we realized they reeked of dog pee. We scrubbed the cupboard with bleach, the broom, and the mop. The fear and disgust subsided, and we started to inspect the place. The dishes had food stuck to them, and when we took them out, the kitchen cabinets were covered in filth. The mattress covers were covered in small pee stains—I assume from a small dog that had been lying there before us, since the owner allows pets. The blinds everywhere hadn't been cleaned in years, but that's the only thing we didn't fix; we didn't care. The bathroom towels were ancient and worn, smelling of mildew; the kitchen towel was shameful; the cutlery, even after boiling and washing it, couldn't get rid of the caked-on grime, so we opted for plastic cutlery; the sheets looked terrible, also very worn and used. When you plugged in the toaster, the power would trip; the TV remote only worked intermittently; the TV was terrestrial, so you could only get a few channels, and the signal kept cutting out; the bedroom fans were laughable—dirty, old, and missing their casings; all the pans were old and sticky; we opened the kitchen extractor fan, and it wouldn't close again; the sink had a bucket underneath to catch the water that overflowed from the drain when washing up, so you had to empty it constantly; the washing machine leaked; in short, it was a disaster in terms of both maintenance and cleanliness, and we paid 120 euros a night! By the way, don't even think about the sofa bed they advertise as sleeping two extra in the apartment. We didn't use it, but it was completely sagging! I absolutely do not recommend renting this house. The owner claimed we hadn't called him during our stay to tell him about all this, but we did call him about the leaky range hood and the overflowing sink. He told us to tighten the drain, which we did, but the water kept leaking. This guy never called us to ask if the problem was fixed; he showed no interest in the matter. As for the cleaning, since he was the cleaner, and seeing the state of everything, we decided to do it ourselves. We were traveling with our baby and didn't trust his cleaning methods. If he had to repair everything individually, it would have kept us busy for the entire 13 days of our stay. So, we decided to take a deep breath and try to enjoy our vacation. That said, we're not going to let all these problems go unpunished and will be reporting all the incidents through legal channels.

The worst service I've ever had. We had dinner on Sunday, August 16, 2026.
We went to this restaurant at 9:30 PM and it took a long time for them to come and serve us. When we finally got a table, we ordered our dinner and drinks. They brought the drinks, but after an hour, and seeing other tables arrive after us and receive their food, I went to ask about our dinner. A waiter told me that hamburgers take longer than other dishes. Five minutes later, the food arrived with plates and cutlery (which made no sense). I went to another waiter to ask, and at 10:40 PM this other waiter told us that he had lost our order and had to come back and ask for it again... At 10:40 PM we couldn't go anywhere for dinner or shopping, so we decided to wait... When they brought us the food, much to our dismay, my mother's food was cold, but the most shocking thing was finding four cold potatoes next to the hamburger, and even one that was completely frozen.

Dr. Zorrilla saw me, and despite his friendliness, I won't be returning.

1 - No one has the right to interfere in a patient's personal life; there must be a reason I'm not a mother. I don't have to give explanations.

2 - We are living beings; we feel pain. Tact is not his strong suit.

3 - The organization at reception is appalling. First, he took my information in front of other people. What about confidentiality? All the results of the Pap smears and other tests are on the shelf, unfiled and unclassified. Furthermore, getting them to answer the phone is a miracle. And when they do answer, it would be an even bigger miracle if they could actually give you your test results! I went in July, and I only managed to get my results when I went there in person. On the phone, there was always an excuse: I don't have my computer, it's not working, I can't reach you right now, call me another day, we're not seeing patients today... It's strange that yesterday, while I was waiting in person, they were answering the phone...

Frustrating.

one_star_reviews.text:
An absolutely deplorable and, frankly, shameful experience. At such a painful time as saying goodbye to a loved one, the last thing you expect is to receive the kind of treatment we received here. From the very first moment, we felt very poorly attended to, lacking empathy, and with the feeling that, instead of helping us, they were taking advantage of a situation in which we were completely vulnerable.

The final bill seemed disproportionate and abusive. They charged us amounts that we consider unjustified for various reasons, and, in addition, they told us that we had used the facilities for more hours than allowed. The body arrived at approximately 5:30 a.m., and the burial was at 10:00 a.m., so we were nowhere near 24 hours. Even so, they tried to charge us as if we had used the facilities far more than we actually had.

What we find even more serious is that they accused us of breaking or using things that we didn't break or use. We disagree with these accusations and find it outrageous that, after going through such a painful time, we also have to face these kinds of situations and prices that we consider completely exorbitant.

The treatment we received was appalling, lacking the sensitivity, respect, and humanity one expects from a funeral home, especially in circumstances like these. We left with a profound sense of helplessness, indignation, and disappointment. I would not recommend this place to anyone. At a time like this, they should be there to support you and make things easier, not make you feel like they're trying to take advantage of you and overcharge you for everything.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible experience and total incompetence. I took my car in for an emergency repair because the gear shift rod broke. They charged me €15 to literally put on two cable ties, which broke two hours after I left the shop. Then I took it back for an engine problem. They charged me €35 for the diagnostic and told me the lambda sensor was faulty. I paid €220 to have it replaced, but after 9 hours the light came back on. I took it back and they told me it was the temperature sensor; I paid another €66 to replace it and the light stayed on. Now they're telling me it's the lambda sensor again and making me wait 7 days to look at it again. A real money-grab that blindly replaces parts at the customer's expense without solving the problem.

And on top of that, they're unpleasant and rude. Not recommended at all.

Overpriced
Services

After some time, the car continued to smoke, so I decided to take it to another garage. To my surprise, they opened the hood, moved some hoses, and showed me that one of them was broken, which was causing the smoke.
I find it shameful that they decided to charge for something they didn't even bother to fix or simply didn't bother to look into.

one_star_reviews.text:
This review isn't about the church itself, but about the woman who was guarding it this past Saturday.
As soon as she saw me take out my camera, she told me I'd have to pay her 3 euros, which seems fair enough, it's part of the church's opening policy.
However, these policies have the opposite effect on me; I neither take photos nor leave the donation for opening a church to visitors.

But all of the above is secondary, because once we decided to leave, we told the woman we were going to take photos, and she muttered under her breath: "What cheapskates..." There's little more to add; you should really reconsider who you entrust with opening and guarding the church, even if they are a volunteer.

The moment you arrive, they're having a party you don't understand at all (they start asking you questions as if you were a punching bag, the first being, "Do you have an appointment?"). But these people live off the food of the entire town and they defend their business very well!

They can't even do the most basic thing, like documenting what's happening. Instead, they throw a plate of spaghetti in your face to make you even more confused by their nonsense.

I recommend that you go with your mobile phone and exercise your right to record yourselves, either on video or WhatsApp audio, as evidence (for which you don't need permission). Report it when necessary, sue a system that we maintain with the money we generate, a system that leaves us defenseless and even dares not to record what's happening! What you're going to report! It's unthinkable what these people are doing, but I repeat, when you understand that they're defending themselves, either we all defend each other here or nothing will ever change.

one_star_reviews.text:
We waited an hour for our pizzas, even though the delivery time was supposed to be 30 minutes, from Griñón to Carranque (very close). It turns out they don't hire more delivery drivers, and the few they have are overwhelmed (I was told so). On top of that, they don't even reimburse them for the gas they use in their own vehicles. It's a disgrace. The poor woman had many other orders to deliver, which is why it took so long—of course, she was trying to conserve gas because they don't pay for it. They're working themselves to the bone, and the delivery service, as I said, is terrible, absolutely terrible. I can only imagine how the pizzas would have arrived if I hadn't canceled—hard as a board! To think I was going to pay 30 euros for this... They called me again, insisting on knowing why I canceled, as if that wasn't enough, and added that I gave the wrong address... There are two issues here.

When the delivery driver called me, she said she had just arrived in Carranque town center, thinking I was there, but an hour had already passed!
Secondly, my real address is wrong on Google Maps, and the problem is that if I enter it, it goes all the way to Ugena. Years ago, my address was the one I put yesterday (by the way, that same street still shows up as my address), but the town council decided to name a street in the town center after that street.
So it wasn't my fault either.

But it's very easy to blame the customer. Zero responsibility, zero trust. I will never order from them again, nor will I ever eat at a place where they don't care about their employees' working conditions or providing good customer service, which is what keeps the business going.
I'm giving it one star because the system won't let you give it zero; otherwise, it wouldn't have any.
What a disgrace! In 2026, in Spain.
What a disgusting society.

My mother has been in the hospital for a month recovering from ankle surgery. The truth is, the care home leaves much to be desired, but if you can manage somewhat on your own, it's more or less adequate. What I find intolerable, and I believe is even dangerous negligence, is that outside of visiting hours, which are from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM and from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM, they keep them locked in by floor, unable to use the stairs or elevators. They can't access the building without staff cards, so more than one patient or family member gets trapped in the elevators or on the stairs every day. It's best if there isn't a tragedy, like a small fire or something that requires a quick escape, because no one will get out of there and people will die.

I think it goes against all safety regulations to lock people inside a building without a possible emergency exit.

one_star_reviews.text: Ah, the tax inspectors! Those tireless guardians of fiscal order who demonstrate the same speed and effectiveness as a snail with rheumatism. It's truly touching to see how they talk so much about "fighting fraud" while deliberately ignoring formal complaints that are a year and a half old. They're clearly far too busy chasing after the self-employed person who claimed a two-euro coffee as a tax deduction to waste time investigating a formally reported business. Their capacity for inaction is almost a work of art. They have the evidence right there on the table, ready to go, but they prefer to employ the ostrich technique: burying their heads in the sand and hoping that tax fraud will resolve itself through spontaneous combustion. A bunch of incompetent bureaucrats who only show efficiency when it comes to fleecing the average citizen, but who suffer from selective blindness and abject laziness when the job is done for them. If the Tax Agency's objective is to discourage citizen collaboration and demonstrate blatant incompetence, congratulations, they're doing a fantastic job.

I bought a watch on August 4th and it stopped working on August 9th. I think they probably sold it to me defective, because it's not normal for that to happen so quickly.
I took it back to the store and the saleswoman told me they would have to send it to Seville to be checked.
To this day, I'm still waiting for a response, and it looks like it will take forever. She warned me that it usually takes more than 20 days for the watch to be back in the store, but since they're on vacation, I might be waiting forever... Based on my experience, I will never buy from that store again, or any other "Time Road" store.
The company's policy, in my opinion, leaves much to be desired, to be honest.
If someone had explained to me that it would take so long to resolve a problem (which might even just be a battery replacement, who knows?)... I would have decided against buying the watch there. I absolutely do not recommend buying any of their products. I'm quite disappointed with the treatment I'm receiving.

We were lied to, robbed, and treated terribly.
At the entrance, they told us the first drink after entering the bingo hall was free. After several cards, we received the receipt. We asked the woman handing them out, and she just said "no, no." When we asked for an explanation, she said, "This is a bingo hall. Do I look stupid?" We asked the waiter (the only one who treated us well), and he told us to ask at the bar. Again, the woman implied that we had to play for several hours to get it for free (the complete opposite of what they said at the entrance). After arguing about their contradictions, they gave us one of the several drinks for free.
The service was awful and completely disorganized. We only went to play bingo without buying anything, but thanks to their lies, we ended up spending more money than we planned.

one_star_reviews.text:
I bought a Careway M1 handbike for €1,890 for my wheelchair from this company on 13.07.2026. Their website has information and a video showing how easy it is to assemble the handbike, but I was unable to attach it correctly to my wheelchair or connect the brakes.

I contacted the shop on 17.07.2026.

I have contacted their technical department several times, but in my experience it does not function as a real technical support service. It seems more focused on refusing or delaying help than on solving the customer’s problem.

Update:
After some time, they told me that I need a technician to set it up. They told me to bring it to Alicante, but I do not live in Alicante.

The company I found that can come to my home charges €197 for the installation and checking of the handbike. I do not understand why I should have to pay this additional amount on top of the €1,890 I have already paid for the handbike and my manual wheelchair, especially as I can only use an electric wheelchair for my daily life.

Today is 30.09.2026, and I still cannot use the handbike, return it, or get proper technical assistance from the shop.

The battery had already been activated, so returning it is also complicated.

Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend that customers who need a mobility device carefully consider the level of technical support available before purchasing from this company.

Company to avoid. Very bad experience. The items I purchased on their website indicated delivery in 2 to 7 business days. I made the purchase on August 11th. After paying for the items, I received an email saying that delivery might be delayed. Since I still hadn't received the order by August 28th, and Dortomedical couldn't tell me when I would receive it, as they claimed it depended on the availability of the carrier or the installer (which was never clear to me), I requested a refund. I received a partial refund, as they deducted €150 from the amount paid. Dortomedical's explanation is that the item had already left their warehouse, and the handling fee for canceling an order (which never arrived, and even they didn't know when it would) is €150. For this reason, I do not recommend them.

First of all, I have to say that the theory test went very well; I passed it in a week.
The bad part came with Inma, the practical instructor. She arrived 10 minutes late to the first class, and the dog groomer who parks there told me about it. It's true, she always has problems with the schedule.
She's a person who has absolutely no empathy for the students, even on the road. How can you say, "Disgusting, how I hold the steering wheel all sweaty!" Well, clean it yourself. She's demotivating. Is everything you do wrong a reason to get disqualified? Not to mention talking on your cell phone for 20 minutes. Thank goodness I dropped her and enrolled her in another driving school that makes me feel safe. My daughter drives the car perfectly well with her father; the problem was you. You should have had your license revoked. You were a student yourself; did they really mess with you that much to make you behave like a jerk? I don't recommend it. They rip you off with the practical lessons. There are no examiners. Don't waste your time here, folks. If you know, my husband went there that afternoon with my daughter to change driving schools. They asked for a medical certificate for something. I don't know how they have Inma teaching classes; the things she says make us want to tear our hair out. And she's always late. 20 minutes on her phone is useless.

one_star_reviews.text: Please do not leave your loved ones in this place; there is absolute chaos in everything: medication, clothing, wound care, diaper changes, feeding, repositioning, attention... far too few staff for so many residents. If they are independent, it's one thing, but if not, they are left staring at a wall with zero stimulation. They will deteriorate rapidly. Absolute neglect and lack of care. Zero supervision from aides, nurses, and doctors. Total lack of information.

I'm giving it one star because I have to if I want to write a review.
"Shameful" is an understatement. The neglect shown to my father-in-law, a man with Alzheimer's—well, "had" because sadly he's passed away—was appalling. He arrived at the hospital with ulcers that were gaping holes, and according to the doctor (if you can even call her that), they were already healed. IF YOU CARE ABOUT YOUR ELDERLY, DON'T TAKE THEM THERE. THE TREATMENT WAS AWFUL.
FAREWELL...

one_star_reviews.text:
Very dissatisfied. I renovated my house and hired them to do the kitchen and the doors. In the kitchen, they installed a refrigerator with a broken door. I complained, and they told me they couldn't do anything; it was the responsibility of the technical service. So, without even having set foot in the kitchen, I had to get the refrigerator repaired myself because they washed their hands of it. Also in the kitchen, they installed a countertop that was supposedly heat-resistant and charged me accordingly. However, it cracked as soon as I put a hot pot on it, and when I called the insurance company, there were no replacements because it was a Chinese-made material with no continuous supply, so I had to replace the entire countertop. They, of course, refused to cover it.
Regarding the doors, they recommended a new material that was cheaper than wood. When a flexible hose on the toilet tank broke, it swelled up very quickly. The insurance company's carpenter told me that material was impossible to find because it was cheap and they didn't stock that type of material regularly. I spoke with them and they said they'd come by my house, but they never had time to come, until I got tired of calling them.
My experience with them has been terrible.

one_star_reviews.text:
I believe this is a highly unprofessional firm. They seem to lack a basic understanding of accounting principles and have made numerous errors in their work. We have had to spend countless hours reviewing and correcting their work ourselves, while many outstanding questions remain unanswered.
The firm was hired by our developer, which created a conflict of interest from the outset. We expected them to represent us professionally and defend our interests, especially when conflicts arose with the developer. However, we never saw any serious effort on their part in this regard. They often gave the impression of being reluctant to confront the developer for fear of losing potential future business opportunities.

Their typical response to these types of reviews is: “I would appreciate it if you identified yourself and explained your issue so that I can respond and assist you as you deserve.”

Ironically, that is precisely the problem: the service you deserve never arrives.

You deserve to tarnish your city's name with businesses like this and for tourists to decide not to visit your city again! There are dozens of negative reviews about that business even here. They don't want to deal with it; they're resorting to absurd "procedures" that they know no one will bother with, just to be a deterrent. In that case, we, as consumers and visitors, will expose you here, and your problem will reach a wider audience.

one_star_reviews.text:
The last time I went, it was supposed to be open. We waited until 9:00 PM and nothing. Closed.

Aside from that, the times I've been there, the experience hasn't been pleasant. The waiters are more focused on playing pool than serving the tables. Every time you want to order something, you have to get up and go to the bar, since no one who works there seems to care.
They never brought us anything to snack on with our drinks. At first, I thought it was common, until I saw one of the waiters offering something to another table; they were clearly friends. No one else even smiled.
For such high prices, you expect better service. The area is nice and the place is cool, but it's all for nothing if the service isn't adequate.
I don't know who owns this business... But well, it leaves a lot to be desired. I really don't recommend the place. There are other bars a 10-minute walk away that offer better service and don't charge so much. It's a real shame.

What's happening at this bank is shameful. I've been a customer my whole life and I've never had any problems until now with the new accounts.
Supposedly, if you open a "savings account," you give them a certain amount of notice and they transfer the money to your regular account.
I signed the closure of the savings account, and a week later, after not receiving the money, I called again and insisted, and they just kept giving me the runaround.

It's shameful how they play with people, and as for respect, forget about it.

SHAMEFUL.

Today I went to the car wash tunnel. It cost me 6 euros for a pressure wash, wax, and three drying passes—that's what the instructions sign says. But they're scammers. The wax is nowhere to be found, and there were only two drying passes. I told the girl who was helping me, and first she said the wax tank was full. I explained that I hadn't used any wax, and she replied that she'd let the bosses know. But she wouldn't give me my money back and said that the three drying passes were supposedly on a little sign that nobody sees.
A really bad experience, and I'm a regular customer, which I'll probably stop being. Lately, the fuel has been pretty bad, and even though it's a few cents cheaper than other gas stations in the area, I've stopped liking the quality. So, one less customer.

I enrolled in the Pilates instructor course in April, started studying, and had to stop for a few months. When I decided to resume my studies this August 2026, the virtual campus platform wasn't working, the contact phone numbers weren't listed, and I sent an email but received no response. I requested a refund for my course because I feel it's a scam, and they only responded to the bank, not to my email. In the comments on their Instagram profile, there are many other people affected like me who haven't been able to complete their practical training, are waiting for their certification, or are simply enrolled in a course but don't have the necessary materials to continue studying.

I hope to get my money back so I can invest it in a course that is 100% reliable. The situation is truly deplorable—paying €1000 for a course and being ripped off like this.
